transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-14 11:00 AM PT / Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE); Maya Rodriguez (Parallax Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Parallax Cloud Infra), Nora Patel (Parallax Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is our QBR slash health check for Parallax, really appreciate you making the time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: Hi, Maya here.
[00:10] Liam: Liam on infra.
[00:12] Nora: Nora from security.
[00:15] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: usage and cost trends, reliability incidents and root causes, roadmap asks (private/VPC + model variants), and security questions. Priya will cover adoption metrics, Ethan will talk about the latency incidents.
[00:30] Priya: Cool, I'll start with usage. Overall tokens have grown about 42% quarter over quarter, our top three routes are chat-agent, summarization, and embedding-search. We saw a big spike in April — appears tied to a new marketing campaign that increased chat volume, plus a few heavy batch embedding jobs from the analytics team.
[00:45] Maya: That matches our internal view, the campaign ramped fast. Can you break down per-route cost?
[00:50] Jordan: Yep, we'll share a CSV after the call; quick numbers — chat-agent is ~55% of token spend, embeddings 30%, other routes 15%. Cost per 1M tokens is still competitive but the batch embedding jobs pushed the monthly bill up by ~28% in April.
[01:10] Liam: On infra we noticed QPS jumps caused burst throttling on hosted tier, which contributed to retries and extra tokens. Is there a recommended way to smooth bursts?
[01:20] Ethan: Two mitigations — client side rate limiting and retry backoff to avoid duplicate tokens, and for the server side you can opt into Dedicated or burst-capacity config. We saw multiple clients without exponential backoff, that was the main source of duplicated requests leading to higher cost.
[01:40] Nora: From security standpoint, we need to confirm data residency and retention on hosted API — anything stored in logs? How long for request/response logs?
[01:50] Priya: By default logs are retained for 30 days for troubleshooting; we can set longer retention with enterprise add-ons, and for Private or Dedicated you can have customer-managed retention and KMS for encryption. We'll attach the security pack.
[02:10] Nora: Good. Also need detail on audit logs — show who accessed which route, and SSO/SAML support.
[02:18] Jordan: Yes we support SAML SSO and RBAC, and audit logs are part of the enterprise package. Priya will send the SOC2 & audit log docs after the call.
[02:30] Maya: Can we talk about reliability — we had a couple of 95th and 99th percentile latency spikes in May that impacted user experience?
[02:40] Ethan: Right, we investigated. Around May 12th and May 23rd, a model shard rebalancing plus an unrelated kernel update increased tail latency on the hosted cluster serving the chat-agent model. That led to longer KV cache miss penalties. We rolled back the kernel patch and adjusted the shard balancing policy which mitigated the spikes.
[03:05] Maya: Was there data loss or incorrect outputs?
[03:08] Ethan: No data loss, only higher latency and some client-side timeouts that caused clients to retry. We correlated request IDs and saw duplication from retries. We're recommending enabling idempotency tokens for critical endpoints to prevent duplicate consumption.
[03:30] Liam: Would Dedicated avoid those rebalances?
[03:33] Ethan: Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools so you won't be affected by noisy neighbors or cluster-wide rebalances. It also offers snapshotting and reduced maintenance windows. For guaranteed throughput and predictable P99, we usually recommend Dedicated if you're hitting production SLAs.
[03:50] Jordan: Pricing-wise, we can run a cost model comparing current hosted spend to estimated Dedicated commitment. We'll need your 3-month projected token usage to model.
[03:58] Maya: We'll provide that. One ask from product: we want an option to pin model variants for specific routes — e.g., lighter quantized model for low-latency agent and higher-quality for summaries. How feasible is that routing?
[04:10] Ethan: Completely feasible — we support per-route model pinning and automatic fallback. You can create policies so certain routes use a quantized 4-bit variant and others use full fp16. We can demo routing rules in the follow-up deep dive.
[04:30] Nora: On encryption — we require customer-managed KMS for keys at rest for any production PII. Is that supported for Dedicated or Private?
[04:38] Priya: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations are available for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer server-side encryption but customer-managed KMS is an enterprise option. We'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[04:55] Maya: SLA — our threshold is < 200ms median and P95 < 800ms for chat. We're seeing medians at 160ms except during spikes. Can Redwood help define a path to P95 reliability?
[05:10] Ethan: Absolutely — between prefix caching, batching tuning, and model-variant pinning, we can get P95 consistently under your target. We'll run a benchmark using your prompt set and payload sizes to validate.
[05:28] Jordan: On the roadmap, quick asks from Parallax were: 1) VPC peering / Private pilot, 2) per-route cost attribution in console, 3) longer retention on usage logs, and 4) better observability for KV cache hits. We'll capture those.
[05:44] Maya: For VPC pilot, we want to test end-to-end: VPC peering, KMS integration, and model pinning. Also want expected rollout timeline.
[05:55] Jordan: If we kick off a pilot, typical timeline is 4-6 weeks for VPC setup + initial validation, longer if on-prem hardware is required. Ethan can lead the technical side.
[06:10] Ethan: I'll propose a pilot plan: week 1 network and IAM validation, week 2 deploy private control plane, week 3 run performance benchmarks, week 4 fix issues and handover. We'll supply infra checklist.
[06:25] Nora: During pilot we need penetration testing and clear SLAs for data handling.
[06:30] Priya: We'll include pen-test options and compliance questionnaire. For SOC2 we can provide the report under NDA.
[06:40] Maya: On cost optimization, we want recommendations — you mentioned batch embedding offload and reranking caching?
[06:48] Ethan: Yes: for embeddings, use incremental embedding (only re-embed changed docs), shard embedding jobs and use Dedicated for large offline batches. For chat, enable prefix caching for common prompts and lower max_tokens where possible. Also consider quantized model variants for cheap-but-fast responses.
[07:10] Liam: Any tooling we can use to detect inefficient prompts or runaway token usage?
[07:16] Priya: Console has per-route token breakdown, and Redwood Optimize will flag high-cost prompts and suggest quantization or batching. We'll send a short how-to.
[07:28] Maya: Okay let's recap next steps.
[07:32] Jordan: Recap: Jordan will send usage CSV and cost model, Priya will send SOC2 and security pack, Ethan will schedule Dedicated benchmark and share pilot plan. Maya and team will share example prompts and 3-month usage forecast.
[07:45] Maya: Sounds good. Also can you include a sample pricing delta between hosted and Dedicated for our current usage?
[07:50] Jordan: Yes — I'll include at least two commitment tiers and a break-even analysis.
[07:55] Nora: One more security note — can you confirm whether hosted logs can be disabled for specific routes?
[08:00] Priya: We can disable debug logging per-route; request metadata for billing still retained but we can minimize content in logs. We'll detail that in the security pack.
[08:12] Liam: For the Dedicated benchmark, we should spin up an identical VPC test cluster so network effects are similar.
[08:20] Ethan: Agreed. We'll request temporary credentials and IAM roles for the bench.
[08:28] Jordan: Anything else?
[08:30] Maya: No, that's it from us. Appreciate the follow-up.
[08:33] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts.
